stories.head: Israeli strike on Gaza's Nasser Hospital kills six, including a surgeon
stories.say: An Israeli air strike hit the surgery department of Nasser Hospital in Khan Younis early on Thursday, killing at least six people, including a surgeon, Gaza health authorities say.
stories.stand: Israel's military said Hamas militants were operating from the hospital but gave no evidence.
body: An Israeli air strike hit the surgery department of Nasser Hospital in Khan Younis, southern Gaza, early on Thursday, ABC News and CBS News reported. Gaza's health ministry said at least six people were killed, including a surgeon.

The Israeli military said it struck a senior Hamas commander and other militants operating inside the hospital, which it called a command centre. It released graphics but no further evidence. Hamas called the strike a war crime.
Health authorities say more than 1,600 people have been killed by Israeli fire since the US-backed ceasefire of October 2025. Nasser is one of few functioning hospitals left in Gaza.

stories.head: One killed and four hurt in shooting at Washington gym
stories.say: A gunman killed one person and wounded four at a gym in Washington's Logan Circle area on Thursday morning, then took his own life in a flat above, police said.
stories.stand: Police said the suspect had a dispute with the building's homeowners' association.
body: A gunman opened fire at the Vida Fitness gym in the Logan Circle neighbourhood of Washington DC at about 8am on Thursday, Euronews and ABC News reported. One person was killed and four were injured, one critically.
The suspect barricaded himself in a seventh-floor flat above the gym. Police said he took his own life after negotiators spoke to him for more than an hour.
Acting Police Chief Jeffery Carroll said the man had a conflict with the building's homeowners' association. Nearby schools were placed on alert during the stand-off.

stories.head: Indonesia's vice-president Gibran resigns over diploma row
stories.say: Indonesia's vice-president, Gibran Rakabuming Raka, the son of former president Joko Widodo, resigned on Thursday after courts cast doubt on his high school qualifications.
stories.stand: He quit hours before parliament was due to consider his impeachment; a successor could take up to 60 days to choose.
body: Indonesia's vice-president, Gibran Rakabuming Raka, 39, resigned on Thursday, ABC News reported. He is the son of former president Joko Widodo.

In October the Constitutional Court found no compelling evidence he held a high school diploma, and the Supreme Court later ruled his equivalency certificate invalid. More than 120 politicians had petitioned for his impeachment, and he quit hours before the House was due to meet on it.
President Prabowo Subianto accepted the resignation. No successor has been named; the assembly's speaker, Ahmad Muzani, said the process could take up to 60 days.

stories.head: Xi Jinping says Taiwan's 'complete reunification' will happen
stories.say: China's President Xi Jinping said on Thursday that Taiwan's complete reunification with China will happen, as Taiwan reported twenty-nine Chinese aircraft and ships around the island.
stories.stand: Taiwan's Mainland Affairs Council rejected Beijing's 'one country, two systems' model.
body: Chinese President Xi Jinping said on Thursday that Taiwan's complete reunification with China will happen, Al Jazeera reported. He spoke at the Great Hall of the People at an event marking 160 years since Sun Yat-sen's birth.

Xi urged peaceful reunification under the one country, two systems model and did not mention force, which Beijing has never ruled out. Taiwan's defence ministry reported 29 Chinese military aircraft and ships on a joint combat readiness patrol around the island.
Taiwan's Mainland Affairs Council rejected the model, saying it would mean submitting to Communist Party rule. Xi is due to meet Donald Trump at the APEC summit in Shenzhen next week.

stories.say: Yemen's Houthis say they attacked Saudi oil and military sites on Thursday, as the UN Security Council voted unanimously to extend sanctions on Yemen for a year.
stories.stand: Saudi Arabia's coalition said it intercepted suspected Houthi drones over Riyadh and the Eastern Province.
body: Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said the group's drones targeted a pumping station on the East-West Pipeline, the Yanbu oil facility and military sites, Al Jazeera reported. The claims could not be independently verified.
Saudi-led coalition spokesman Major General Turki al-Maliki said suspected Houthi drones were intercepted over the Riyadh region and Eastern Province on Thursday.
The same day, the UN Security Council voted unanimously to extend Yemen sanctions, including asset freezes and travel bans, for one year, along with the mandate of its panel of experts.

stories.head: Russian rights lawyer jailed for 12 years for treason
stories.say: A court in Kaliningrad has jailed the sixty-six-year-old rights lawyer Maria Bontsler for twelve years for treason, accused of passing information to Ukraine.
stories.stand: Rights group Slovo Zashchite said the trial was held behind closed doors.
body: A court in Russia's Baltic exclave of Kaliningrad sentenced rights lawyer Maria Bontsler, 66, to 12 years in prison for treason on Thursday, Al Jazeera reported. Prosecutors had sought 15 years.
She was accused of passing information to Ukraine from 2024 about Kaliningrad security officers and criminal cases. She had worked with people accused of political offences.
The rights group Slovo Zashchite said the trial was closed. Her lawyers argued the information was not secret and said she was in poor health.

stories.head: Fourteen killed in multi-vehicle crash in the UAE
stories.say: Fourteen people were killed and thirty injured when a lorry lost control at the entrance to Fujairah in the United Arab Emirates, setting off a crash involving eighteen vehicles.
stories.stand: The UAE Interior Ministry said the lorry caught fire and flames spread to other vehicles.
body: Fourteen people were killed and 30 injured in a crash at the entrance to the emirate of Fujairah shortly before midnight, the UAE Interior Ministry said, Al Jazeera reported.
A lorry driver lost control and hit another vehicle, and both struck stationary traffic. The lorry caught fire and the flames spread. Eighteen vehicles, five of them lorries, were involved.
Those killed included Emirati and foreign nationals, and DNA tests are under way. Fifteen of the injured have been discharged.

stories.head: Migrant caravan sets off from southern Mexico

stories.stand: It is the third caravan since September; a Chiapas official put its size at about 1,500.
body: More than 1,000 migrants, mostly Central American, set out from Tapachula near the Guatemalan border on Tuesday, Al Jazeera reported. A Chiapas state government source estimated about 1,500, including many families.
They are heading for Mexico City, more than 1,000 km away, to seek help and protection from detention. It is the third caravan since September.
Donald Trump warned Mexico to stop the group or face doubled tariffs. A separate group of about 100 migrants was blocked on Tuesday.

stories.say: Pope Leo the Fourteenth has begun a six-day visit to Peru, where he served for years. The Vatican estimates about three million people lined his route in Lima.
stories.stand: It is the last leg of a Latin American tour that took in Uruguay and Argentina.
body: Pope Leo XIV arrived in Lima on Wednesday for a six-day visit to Peru, which he calls his second homeland, Euronews and CBS News reported. He was born in Chicago.

About three million people lined his motorcade route, according to Vatican estimates. He told authorities he was also returning to his homeland and urged Peru to confront its painful history with justice.
The visit is the final leg of a Latin American tour after Uruguay and Argentina. He will visit Cuzco and Chiclayo, where he was bishop for a decade.

stories.say: Spain's parliament has narrowly approved wider eviction protections for vulnerable tenants by thirty-five votes to thirty-four, a day after a general strike over housing costs.
stories.stand: A second measure, limiting purchases by property firms, was rejected by the same margin.
body: Spain's interim lower house ratified a decree on Thursday extending eviction protections for tenants judged financially or socially vulnerable, Al Jazeera reported. The vote was 35 to 34.
A separate measure barring property firms from buying homes below 70% of their value was rejected by 34 votes to 35.
The vote followed Wednesday's general strike over rents and living costs. The conservative Popular Party says it will repeal the measures if it wins the snap election this month.

body: Canada will bar Russian and Belarusian athletes and officials from entering to compete at the IIHF World Junior Championship in Alberta, even if they hold valid visas, Al Jazeera reported. The event runs from 26 December to 5 January.
Secretary of State for Sport Adam van Koeverden said Canada opposed their participation while Russia continues its war against Ukraine. Hockey Canada backs the government.
The Court of Arbitration for Sport had ruled that the IIHF must admit Russian teams to five championships, starting with this one.

Elisabeth Diatta, 16, won the women's 55kg beach wrestling title and Maguette Diop, 16, won the boys' 80kg. Ndeye Khady Anna Diatta took gold at 45kg.

stories.head: Surveyors' outlook for house sales weakest since July 2023
stories.say: Property surveyors expect home sales to fall over the next year, with the weakest outlook since July twenty twenty-three, according to the Royal Institution of Chartered Surveyors.
stories.stand: A net 36% of surveyors saw prices fall in October, with higher mortgage rates weighing on demand.
body: A net 17% of property professionals expect sales to fall over the next year, the weakest outlook since July 2023, according to the Royal Institution of Chartered Surveyors' October survey, ITV News reported.

A net 24% reported falls in both buyer inquiries and agreed sales. A net 36% saw prices fall after a stable summer. London, East Anglia, the West Midlands and the South East were weaker than average, while prices in Northern Ireland kept rising.
RICS said higher mortgage rates were weighing on demand. Its head of market research, Tarrant Parsons, said buyer demand remains subdued.

stories.stand: Three of the men face US charges; officials have not confirmed the wider network.
body: An ITV News investigation, based on conversations with security officials, says seven men ran an alleged network posing as a group called the Islamic Movement of Companions of the Right, which officials believe worked for Iranian intelligence.
Alleged attacks include a synagogue bombing in Liège, arson on Hatzola ambulances in Golders Green, London, on 23 March, and an attempt to target RAF Fairford.

Three of the men face an eight-count US indictment unsealed in New York on Tuesday. The other findings are ITV's and have not been confirmed officially. Iran has denied involvement in the Fairford plot.

body: A study of 844,108 adults in China, the UK, the US and Spain, published in Nature, tested a framework that separates clinical obesity from preclinical obesity, Euronews reported.

stories.say: The Princess of Wales says nature played a major part in her recovery from cancer, in an interview with Robert Macfarlane for Country Life magazine.
stories.stand: She also spoke of her concern about rising anxiety among children.
body: The Princess of Wales told the author Robert Macfarlane that nature played a major role in her recovery from cancer, in an interview for Country Life's special edition guest-edited by the Prince of Wales, ABC News reported.

She said she was told in hospital that recovery would not be linear, and that staying connected to trusted people and peaceful places was important. She announced she was in remission in January 2025.
She also said she was concerned about rising anxiety among children, and that time outdoors can build a sense of belonging.

stories.stand: The club said it would appoint a permanent successor as quickly as possible; no replacement has been confirmed.
body: Manchester United sacked head coach Michael Carrick on Thursday, Al Jazeera and ITV News reported. The club said it would appoint a permanent successor as quickly as possible.
United are 18th in the Premier League with eight points from 10 games, their worst league start in 40 years. Their only league win came against Ipswich Town in August.
